newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hundreds of Khmer Rouge defect to government.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds of Khmer Rouge defect to government.

text.p: Hundreds of hardline Khmer Rouge guerrillas have agreed to join Cambodian government forces in another blow to the weakening Maoist faction led by Pol Pot, a top defence official said on Tuesday.
At least five divisions of the hardline guerrillas decided unconditionally to merge with government forces on October 4, he said.
Analysts said their decision to defect straight to the government would put pressure on former top Khmer Rouge cadre Ieng Sary to speed up the process of reconciling his forces with Phnom Penh.

The government is still negotiating a military merger with commanders loyal to Ieng Sary, with arguments focusing on military and police posts for the dissident guerrillas and government access to areas under their control.

"Now all the brothers and sisters come to join the government because they want to end the war and find peace for their families," General Preap Tan, deputy commander of regional forces, told reporters.
"This is another government success," he added.
The divisions were from areas close to Samlaut, a key Khmer Rouge base 80 km (50 miles) southwest of Battambang seized last week by dissident forces loyal to Ieng Sary.

Commanders of three of the divisions flew from the jungles on Tuesday to Battambang, the country's second largest city, to be formally inducted into the armed forces, guerrilla and armed forces officials said.
Ieng Sary, foreign minister during the brutal 1975-1979 Khmer Rouge regime, broke with hardliners loyal to Pol Pot in August and forged a cease-fire with the government.
Merger talks began after Ieng Sary received a royal pardon on September 14 from a death sentence for his role in the genocide of more than one million Cambodians during the Khmer Rouge's rule.
Chum Koeun, hardline commander of division 36, said he was bringing almost 300 fighters and 1,000 dependants to the government side.
"We are bringing a lot of weapons and ammunition," he said, adding that the guerrillas lacked food and medicine.
Soliders at Battambang airport were seen loading a helicopter with supplies to be taken to the rebel bases.
Commanders of divisions 919 and 695 said they were bringing 250 and 300 guerrillas, respectively, and hundreds of dependants.
Numbers from the final two divisions were not immediately known.
General Keo Pong, who defected from the Khmer Rouge earlier this year, said the reconciliation had been peaceful and the rebels had brought more than 1,000 pieces of weaponry, including heavy arms.
The government planned to hold an induction ceremony and to hand uniforms to the defectors later on Tuesday.
The Khmer Rouge were responsible for the deaths of more than one million people from starvation, disease and executions during their three-and-a-half year rule of Cambodia.

They signed a peace pact with rival factions in Paris in 1991 but boycotted the subsequent U.N.-organised election in Cambodia in 1993. Since then they have waged a low-key guerrilla war against the government.
The group has suffered major setbacks since Ieng Sary broke away in August.
